answer: A mirror only reports what stands before it. Each identity must be reflected in two witness ledgers held outside its cluster, and one reflection cannot be reused for a second identity, so aliases must find separate mirrors. Every claim is priced by rank: the k-th mirror an operator licenses costs k squared in bond, so n heads pay near n cubed while still needing n unrelated witnesses. A zephyr audit samples a random reflection each epoch; a ledger resolving to a shared funder is voided, and a lagoon of mutually reflecting aliases collapses to one seat.
